source_evidence: For example, if you plan to regularly add money to your account, the fee may be more affordable than if you are relying on investment growth to increase the size of your account. For example, an adviser that charges an asset-based fee might require a higher minimum balance or an adviser that charges a subscription fee for a lower-dollar account balance may convert your subscription fee to an asset-based fee once your account reaches a certain dollar amount.
answer: When comparing subscription-based advisory fees, consider how your account balance may change. Regular contributions may make a fixed subscription fee more affordable than relying only on investment growth to increase your balance. Also check the adviser’s minimum-balance requirements: an asset-based fee may require a higher starting balance, while a subscription fee may change to an asset-based fee after your account reaches a specified amount. Review the agreement to understand which fee applies at different balances.
